brief: Goldman's 2027 Global Credit Outlook forecasts negative USD IG excess returns (-0.5% versus a +2.0% post-GFC median) and near-zero USD HY returns (+0.3% versus a 5.6% median), because record AI-related bond supply is concentrated at the top of the rating stack. Hyperscalers' negative 3Q2026 free cash flow has made debt-market access a competitive advantage, driving $2.4tn of 2027 USD IG gross supply (two-thirds of this year's jumbo deals AI-related) and pushing AAA/AA issuers to a record 22% share of USD IG supply, which has cheapened the safest rating bucket (USD AA spreads moved from the 9th to the 50th percentile since January). Because AI-exposed names now sit in the highest-rated cohort, Goldman recommends moving down in quality: buying BBBs over AAA/AA/A, and single-Bs over BBs, while shifting from neutral to preferring IG over HY overall (a call Morgan Stanley also made this week). Goldman stays underweight Technology, overweight Banks/Energy/Health Care, cautious on European AT1s into French elections, and expects default rates and recovery values to worsen modestly. Because 2026's pain stayed contained to AI names and CCCs, Goldman argues 2027's AI risks (capacity constraints, monetization shortfalls) are more likely to spread into broader macro weakness, so it recommends keeping cheap macro hedges and resetting them into year-end strength.
